_comment: Critical voter-service facts. Only a human editor changes this file, with CODEOWNER review. CI fails if data.js differs from these values.

values.dates[0].pastNote: Closed for this election. You can still check your status.
values.dates[1].s: Your mailed application must arrive by this date
values.dates[2].s: Last day to hand in an application at your county’s absentee office
values.dates[3].s: By hand: before your county office closes. By mail: it must arrive by noon Nov 3.
values.dates[3].pastNote: Hand delivery has closed. A mailed ballot counts only if it arrives by noon Nov 3.
values.absenteeStages[0].title: Can’t make it to the polls on Nov. 3?
values.absenteeStages[0].text: You may qualify to vote absentee if you’ll be out of your county (including at college), work a required shift of 10 hours or more during polling hours, are ill or disabled, or care for a homebound family member. Mailing an application now is risky: it must arrive by Tue, Oct. 27. The safer route is to apply in person at your county’s absentee office by Thu, Oct. 29.
values.absenteeStages[1].title: Need an absentee ballot?
values.absenteeStages[1].text: The mail deadline has passed. If you qualify, you can still apply in person at your county’s absentee office through Thu, Oct. 29.
values.absenteeStages[2].title: Voting on Tuesday, Nov. 3
values.absenteeStages[2].text: Regular absentee applications are closed. Already have a ballot? Return it by hand before your county’s absentee office closes Mon, Nov. 2, or by mail so it arrives by noon Nov. 3. A medical emergency or unexpected work trip may still qualify you for an emergency absentee ballot; ask your county’s absentee election manager right away. Otherwise, vote at your polling place on Tuesday, Nov. 3, from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

vote[0].p: The deadline to register for this election was Monday, Oct. 19. Look up your registration, district, polling place, and sample ballot.

vote[1].p: Tuesday, Nov. 3, from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. If you’re in line by 7 p.m., you can vote.
list: Alabama has no early voting. Voting before Election Day means voting absentee, which requires a qualifying reason.
Some polling places near the Georgia line may run on Eastern Time (7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Eastern). Check with your county if unsure.
Moved within your county since you registered? Go to the polling place for your new address, update your registration there, and vote a provisional ballot.
Moved to another county? Call your county Board of Registrars before Election Day.
Alabama driver’s license or nondriver ID
Free Alabama Photo Voter ID card, available from your county Board of Registrars, even on Election Day
U.S. passport, military ID, or tribal ID
Other photo ID issued by Alabama, another state or the federal government, such as a pistol permit or a Department of Corrections release ID
Employee photo ID from the federal government or from an Alabama state, county or city government
Student or employee ID from an Alabama college, or from a public college in another state
vote[2].after: Bring the physical card; digital IDs, including Alabama’s digital driver’s license, are no longer accepted. A license expired less than 60 days still counts.

vote[3].p: You need a qualifying reason. The most common:
list: You’ll be out of your county on Election Day, including at college or in the military
You have a required work shift of 10 hours or more that overlaps polling hours
You’re ill or have a disability that keeps you from the polls
You’re caring for a family member who is confined at home
You’re a poll worker at a polling place other than your own

deadlines.caption: Absentee deadlines for Nov. 3

rows.h: By hand (at your county’s absentee office)
c: Mon, Nov 2, before the office closes (5 p.m. at the latest)

deadlines.note: The mail and hand deadlines flip: a mailed application is due first, but a mailed ballot is due last.

ol: Get the application for the county where you’re registered: download it, ask your county’s absentee election manager (usually the circuit clerk), or call 334‑242‑7210.
Return it yourself with a copy of your photo ID: by mail so it arrives by Tue, Oct 27, or in person by Thu, Oct 29. Some county offices let you apply and vote in one visit; call ahead.
Mark your ballot and sign the affidavit in front of a notary or two witnesses age 18 or older. Without this, your ballot can’t be counted.

Return the ballot yourself: by hand before your county’s absentee office closes on Mon, Nov 2 (5 p.m. at the latest), or by mail or a carrier such as FedEx or UPS so it arrives by noon Tue, Nov 3. Except in a medical emergency, no one else may return it for you.
vote[3].after: Time is short: the Secretary of State advises mailing at least two weeks before each deadline, so applying in person by Thu, Oct 29 is the safer route. College students: apply to the county where you’re registered, and use the form’s mailing-address line to have the ballot sent where you get mail. Had a medical emergency, or an unexpected work trip out of your county, after the deadline? You may qualify for an emergency absentee ballot. Ask your county’s absentee election manager right away: work-trip applications close at 5 p.m. Mon, Nov 2, and medical-emergency ballots are due by noon Tue, Nov 3. Military and overseas voters apply by the same dates, but their ballots count if postmarked by Nov 3 and received by noon Tue, Nov 10.

vote[4].p: Two poll workers who know you can sign a sworn statement identifying you, and you can vote a regular ballot. Otherwise, you can vote a provisional ballot, which counts once officials confirm you’re eligible; to have it counted, bring a valid photo ID to your county Board of Registrars by 5 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6.

vote[5].p: Call the Secretary of State’s Elections Division at 334‑242‑7210 (toll-free 1‑800‑274‑8683), or your county Board of Registrars.

callout.title: Can’t make it to the polls on Nov. 3?
callout.text: You may be able to vote absentee if you’ll be out of your county (including away at college), work a required shift of 10 hours or more during polling hours, are ill or disabled, or care for a homebound family member. Mailed applications must arrive by Tuesday, Oct. 27, and the ballot needs a notary or two witnesses.

idCard.title: Bring a photo ID
idCard.text: A physical photo ID, such as a driver’s license or a free Alabama Photo Voter ID. No ID? Two poll workers who know you can sign a statement identifying you, or you can vote a provisional ballot and show ID by 5 p.m. Fri, Nov. 6.
